report.summary: Reviewed LanguageSpec registry chunk; all claims about fields and backends are uncheckable or consistent with code.

handoff.purpose: Define LanguageSpec dataclass and registry of language entries.

symbols.name: LanguageSpec
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding per-language facts: name, extensions, comment delimiters, string delimiters, tree-sitter grammar, function/import types, guard keywords, safety content regexes.

symbols.name: _rx
symbols.note: Helper to compile multiple regex patterns into a tuple.

symbols.name: _SPECS
symbols.note: Tuple of LanguageSpec entries for Python, C, C++, Java, Rust, Go.

claims.text: Adding a language is *data*, not code: one ``LanguageSpec`` entry.
claims.why: The chunk defines LanguageSpec as a frozen dataclass and populates _SPECS with entries, consistent with the claim.

claims.text: Fields are consumed by three backends: the stdlib/lexical path (always available) uses ``line_comment`` / ``block_comment`` / ``guard_keywords`` for comment-aware metrics and the universal windowed clone pass;
claims.why: The claim describes usage of fields by backends not present in this chunk.

claims.text: the tree-sitter path (optional) uses ``ts_grammar`` + ``function_types`` + ``import_types`` for precise unit-level extraction;
claims.why: No tree-sitter backend code in this chunk.

claims.text: the safety fence uses ``safety_content`` regexes to raise the risk tier (Rust ``unsafe``, C register writes, …) on top of the path-based fence.
claims.why: No safety fence code in this chunk.

claims.text: Default covers the C family; override where ' is not a string opener -- Rust lifetimes ('a) and Swift, where consuming to the next ' would eat code.
claims.why: Rust entry sets string_delims=('"',), overriding default; Swift not present but claim only says 'override where ...', consistent.

claims.text: Node-type names follow the corresponding tree-sitter grammar; they are only read when tree-sitter is installed.
claims.why: No tree-sitter reading code in this chunk.

observations.what: All defined LanguageSpec entries have consistent field types and match the dataclass definition.
